_: Files that still hardcode a deployed contract address, and the retired addresses that must never reappear. Enforced by scripts/check-no-hardcoded-addresses.sh, in BOTH directions: an undeclared file carrying an address fails, and a declared file that no longer carries one fails too, so this list can only shrink.
_howToClear: Read the address from configuration - env for a backend or portal, the deploy ledger (scripts/lib/ledger.sh) for tooling, the generated bundle for the phones - then delete the entry here, in the SAME change. Three entries are documentation whose addresses are HISTORICAL RECORDS rather than guidance and are expected to stay; the rest are open findings with the work named in their own reason.
_retiredIsNoLongerTheWholeSet: The gate DERIVES the superseded set from the ledger's own git history (chainId-filtered) - see the header of scripts/check-no-hardcoded-addresses.sh for why. `retired` below is now for addresses the ledger NEVER published, e.g. a per-record-type clone provisioned by scripts/demo-provision-government.sh. Entries that history already covers are kept deliberately: they cost nothing, and they mean a history problem degrades to the old behaviour rather than to none. Do NOT prune them.

stillHardcoded.packages/ui/src/schema/demoData.ts: OPEN FINDING, not an accepted exception - surfaced the moment the gate started deriving the retired set from ledger history. DEMO_ISSUER_APPLICATION_VET/GROOMER put the RETIRED DEPLOYER EOA 0x119F8c7F... into the admin issuer-application form. It is the wrong value twice over: AGENTS.md requires demo values to be unmistakably fake, and that EOA is emphatically NOT inert - a 2026-07-16 audit found it still holds the retired SBT's ISSUER_ROLE and known record-type whitelists, so a demo fill hands a real still-privileged key to a real registrar form. Replace it with an unmistakably-fake address. Deliberately NOT changed here: it is product data, and this change is the gate.
stillHardcoded.stacks/admin/web/src/lib/governance.ts: STAYS. FORMER_DEPLOYER_EOA is a DENYLIST entry, not a lookup: it names one specific historical key so the UI can warn that it no longer holds governance authority. Sourcing it from configuration would make the warning configurable, which defeats it. Same class as the ceremony transcripts - the value is the record.
stillHardcoded.stacks/government/web/e2e/oversight.spec: OPEN FINDING. A fixture uses the retired deployer EOA as an event `actor`. Harmless today (the spec mocks and asserts only rendering), but it is a real address in a fixture, and AGENTS.md's rule is that a fixture must come from what the emitter really produces rather than from a value that reads plausible. Replace with an unmistakably-synthetic actor; needs the spec re-run, so it is not folded into the gate change.
stillHardcoded.AGENTS.md: STAYS. Mixes deployment provenance (M3/M5 records, the r8 redeploy) with live guidance. Provenance legitimately pins the instance it describes; live guidance points at the ledger. Point new live guidance at the ledger, leave provenance alone.
stillHardcoded.docs/CEREMONY_TRANSCRIPT.consent.md: STAYS. A ceremony transcript attests to the instance it names; one that stopped naming it would stop being a transcript. Historical record, not guidance.
